purpose: Demonstrate the minimum semantic decomposition needed to replace lossy article-level EXTREQ representations. This file does not allocate replacement EXTREQ identities and is not a substitute for specialist legal assurance.

tested_records.reason: Article 10 contains multiple independently assessable duties and applicability conditions. One generic data-governance summary cannot identify which proposition was satisfied or breached.

candidate_constituent_propositions.summary: Where covered high-risk AI systems use model-training techniques with data, development must use training, validation and testing datasets meeting the applicable quality criteria.
Training, validation and testing datasets must be subject to data-governance and management practices appropriate to the intended purpose.
The data-governance practices must address relevant design choices.
The data-governance practices must address data-collection processes and data origin, including the original collection purpose for personal data.
The data-governance practices must address relevant data-preparation operations such as annotation, labelling, cleaning, updating, enrichment and aggregation where applicable.
The data-governance practices must address assumptions about what the data are intended to measure and represent.
The data-governance practices must assess the availability, quantity and suitability of the datasets needed.

Datasets must be examined for relevant possible biases capable of affecting health or safety, fundamental rights or prohibited discrimination, including feedback effects where outputs influence future inputs.
Appropriate measures must be taken to detect, prevent and mitigate possible biases identified through the required examination.
Training, validation and testing datasets must satisfy the applicable relevance, representativeness, error and completeness/statistical-property criteria for the intended purpose.
Datasets must account, to the extent required by intended purpose, for characteristics particular to the geographical, contextual, behavioural or functional setting of intended use.
For covered high-risk systems not using model-training techniques, the specified Article 10 dataset obligations apply only to testing datasets as provided by the consolidated text.

tested_records.reason: Article 13 contains a transparency design duty, a distinct instructions-for-use quality duty and multiple mandatory information elements. A single article-level summary cannot support clause-level assessment.

candidate_constituent_propositions.summary: High-risk AI systems must be designed and developed with sufficient operational transparency to enable deployers to interpret outputs and use the system appropriately.
High-risk AI systems must be accompanied by instructions for use in an appropriate format that are concise, complete, correct, clear, relevant, accessible and comprehensible to deployers.
Instructions for use must identify the provider and provide contact details, and where applicable identify the authorised representative.

Instructions for use must provide the prescribed characteristics, capabilities and performance limitations, including intended purpose and applicable accuracy, robustness and cybersecurity information and foreseeable circumstances affecting them.
Instructions for use must provide the source-prescribed information needed to enable deployers to interpret outputs and implement the applicable human-oversight measures.
Where prescribed by Article 13(3), instructions must provide relevant computational and hardware requirements and other technical information necessary for proper system use.

migration_rule: Where canonical re-extraction confirms independently assessable propositions, retire the coarse requirement identity and allocate deterministic replacement identities; where a source-defined compound should remain one unit, preserve identity and store constituents explicitly.
